changelog: v353: a telling of an episode keeps its kind, and one bad node never stops the drawing. WHERE IT WAS SEEN: the owner's own vault, on staging, with the v352 pin ALREADY LIVE when the defect was found — the daily maintenance scheduler was paused to keep the broken path off his vault, and it stays paused until this deploys. v352's `place-answers` read 28 promoted answers carrying a card, placed 1 from the recency reading and filed 7 as `telling_only`. One of those seven was his reply "This happened in the middle of sixth grade for James." (`sources/conversations/msg-3737a80061e5fd4938204b9b.md`, `session_ref: conversation:cand:work_item:work:2f5dec9f0e57ad5a31b9947a`), filed as `claim:cb8c3d3dd46438ea6a76720d`, an `occurrence` on `node:22784323839a0481b081ceab` — "James Everett moved between baseball teams". That node is an EPISODE: `episode:59ae397ae9edf8b6719355f7`, a deterministic `create` over two classification tellings, canonical kind `moment`, one of its tellings' claims (`claim:d7232eaa701b0f24d60a7356`) still in the index. The next `temporal_publication.publish` RAISED `temporal_projection.TimelineNodeError: episode_block_on_non_episode_node: node:22784323839a0481b081ceab carries an episode_id but its node_kind is 'event'` and DREW NOTHING AT ALL — not one bad node, no projection, which on the hosted platform parks the compile job so the vault stops updating for everything. THE CAUSE: the fold had TWO readings of "is this node an episode?" and they were asked of different things. `temporal_timeline._group_claims` created the group for a node id from the first claim it read and asked `episode_fold.EpisodeIdentity.episode_node_for` — a question about THAT CLAIM, *did a bind put this telling in an episode?* The answer's telling is bound to nothing (no rung has looked at it, and `answer_placement` is a claim filer and not an identity decider), and it created the group only because its claim id sorts first: `temporal_store.active_claims` is in claim-id order and `claim:cb8c3d…` precedes `claim:d7232e…`. So the group was made an `event`. `EpisodeIdentity.node_block` then read the PUBLISHED episode↔node map, which knows nothing about claim order, and stamped the episode block on it — and `temporal_projection.validate_calculated_timeline_node` refused the shape, correctly, for the reason its own comment gives: `node_kind` is INSIDE the node id's digest (`NODE_IDENTITY_KEYS`), so the two cannot disagree without one of them being a fabrication. THE RULE (`episode_fold.AN_EPISODE_NODES_KIND_IS_THE_NODES_AND_NOT_ITS_FIRST_CLAIMS`): an episode's node id is minted WITH `node_kind: episode` inside its digest (`episode_fold_contract.episode_node_id`), so a group drawn at that id IS that episode whatever its claims say and whichever of them was read first. There is now ONE reading — `EpisodeIdentity.episode_of`, asked of the NODE ID — and both the grouping and the episode block go through it, so the two cannot disagree and the fold cannot draw a node the projection must refuse. The group also takes the episode's own `canonical_event_kind` on that reading rather than only on the bind's, which is where §3.2 always said it comes from. It is gated on the same `active` flag `node_block` is gated on, so CERT-11's "delete the layer and the drawing returns" is unchanged: a vault with no active binding does no identity work at all and every such node still draws as an `event`. THE WRITER IS RIGHT AS IT STANDS, and that was the other half worth deciding: a telling of an episode is NOT refused and there is no `card_is_an_episode` refusal. The repeat kinds are exactly where "when did X happen?" cards cluster (`identity_resolution.REPEATABLE_EVENT_KINDS` — moves, jobs, schools, teams, residences; two of the owner's own seven tellings land on episode nodes), so refusing would drop his answers for the commonest card class there is, and it would contradict the module's own receipt: `answer_placement.answer_telling_ref` already declares the reply as v337's unit, one fact inside one message, keyed on the NODE's digest so two answers to one card are two tellings of the same fact. Two things are load-bearing for that and are now written down in `answer_placement`'s own docstring so they are not re-litigated: `answer_claim` takes `event_kind` from the CARD's node, which for an episode is that episode's canonical kind, so the claim never argues with the node about what it is; and the telling is DECLARED and not BOUND, because whether it is the same event stays `episode_binder`'s decision under Law 6 (a miss is cheap, a wrong link is not) — the episode's `tellings`, `telling_count` and `identity_origins` are untouched and the new claim is simply another published input. AND THE DRAWING NOW FAILS SOFT FOR THIS CLASS. `temporal_timeline._node_dict_or_finding` catches exactly `temporal_projection.EPISODE_BLOCK_ON_NON_EPISODE_NODE` — newly named so the repair matches a constant rather than a string literal, with `test_temporal_projection.raised_finding_codes` taught to resolve a module-level binding so there is still ONE definition of the id — draws the node as the episode its id says it is, and reports `episode_node_kind_redrawn` (`DIAGNOSTIC_EPISODE_NODE_REDRAWN`). The precedent is `landmark_projection`'s refusals and v340's `owner_birth_anchor_ambiguous`: an invalid shape from a legitimate filing is a FINDING about ONE node, never an exception that stops the drawing of every other one. It is NARROW on purpose — every other member of `ERROR_CODES` still stops the drawing, because those mean the fold computed something it cannot explain, and the repaired node is re-validated so a shape that is wrong in a second way still refuses. The belt is kept although grouping now agrees, because `publish` raising is not one bad node: it is the whole vault, which is what this incident was. `CALCULATION_RULE_VERSION` DOES NOT MOVE, and it is PROVED rather than argued: two fresh scratch clones of the owner's vault at the same head, one with v352 bytes and one with v353's, publish BYTE-IDENTICAL `calculated-timeline.json` and `work-items.json` (generation 187, 1265 nodes, 69 work items). Every input the new reading touches used to produce NO drawing at all, so no vault whose head has not moved draws anything different and no golden moves. MEASURED on a FRESH scratch clone of the owner's vault (`origin/main` at `ae6931b0`, generation 187, the v353 framework overlaid, a full rebuild and publish before and after so both readings are the same kind; the original was never written to). `place-answers --dry-run` and the write agree exactly: 28 answers with a card, 1 placed (`recency_and_capture_date`), 7 `telling_only`, 20 refused `card_not_published`, no errors. Then PUBLISH SUCCEEDS — generation 187 -> 188, nodes 1265 -> 1263, node kinds episode 882 -> 881 / event 378 -> 377 / period 5 -> 5, episode blocks 761 -> 761, `node_aliases` 1028 -> 1028, placed nodes 1215, open cards 69 -> 66 (precision_gap 47 -> 45, missing_anchor 8 -> 7, contradiction 11, place_ambiguous 2, identity_uncertain 1). The owner's cussing answer PLACES from the recency reading: `node:3380558928426602253447c7` "Harvey's love of cussing" renders "24 July 2026-24 September 2026 - you said last month, told 2026-09-24", basis `explicit`. All 7 `telling_only` filings land and NO node's kind breaks — the two that target episodes (`node:22784323839a0481b081ceab` "James Everett moved between baseball teams" and `node:d3676d57ae13802ee082a055` "Father moves between family homes sick") both keep `node_kind: episode` with their `episode_id`, and no published node whose id the identity layer knows is drawn as anything else. `episode_node_kind_redrawn` fires ZERO times, which is the point: a telling of an episode is an ordinary thing for a person to file, so grouping gets it right and the belt stays silent. ONE THING THE VERIFICATION FOUND THAT IS NOT THIS DEFECT, AND IT IS FILED RATHER THAN SWALLOWED (lifehug#409): the v340/v342 audit over the whole act is NOT empty — `{"lost": ["node:091ec8a898daa8548afaf104"], "moved": [], "drawn_at_an_alias": []}`. `temporal_store._fold` step 1 elects ONE winning receipt per `(source_id, revision)` and marks every other receipt's claims `superseded / reextracted`, and v352's `file_answer` writes its receipt on the promoted reply ITSELF — so on the two answered messages that already carried a `general_listener` receipt, the answer's receipt won the group and retired the listener's reading of the same words: `claim:36bae1eb0bbfd2120274471d` (a `graduation` date, 2006, mention `Katie Ann Merrill`) took `node:091ec8a898daa8548afaf104` and its 2006 placement with it, and `claim:257f9e5681424bdd8539c76a` took the undated `node:3d1065f366b17440103c9a25`. That is v352's, not this release's — `system/temporal_store.py` is untouched here and `answer_placement.py`'s only diff is documentation — and fixing it means moving the election unit to `(source_id, revision, extractor_version)`, which moves the fold for every vault and wants its own release and its own audit. Under v352 that vault had no drawing at all, so v353 is strictly better on it; the gap is named, measured and tracked. The audit over the two derivations that differ ONLY by this release's reading — same claims, same records — is empty, and the synthetic whole-act audit is empty. GUARDS: `tests/test_v353_a_telling_of_an_episode_keeps_its_kind.py` — 35 tests on a synthetic vault whose ids are the owner's own, because content addressing means an episode built from the same two telling refs about the same subject mints `episode:59ae397ae9edf8b6719355f7`, is drawn at `node:22784323839a0481b081ceab`, carries `work:2f5dec9f0e57ad5a31b9947a` and receives `claim:cb8c3d3dd46438ea6a76720d` from that reply, with the card minted by the REAL minter (`temporal_publication.publish`). The defect REPRODUCED first — the whole file run against v352 bytes fails 24 tests, ten of them with the exact `episode_block_on_non_episode_node` on the exact node id — and the fixture ASSERTS the condition it needs rather than assuming it (the index is in claim-id order and the answer's claim is the one that creates the group), so a future change to the claim digest fails this file loudly instead of quietly folding the defect away. Then: the node an episode before anybody answers and still an episode after; the reply filed as a telling with no refusal; the claim's kind proved to be the node's; the owner's words on the node; the telling declared and NOT bound (`tellings` and `telling_count` unmoved); the card still open because nobody said when; a DATED answer to the same card placing the episode at 1998-03 and closing its precision_gap; idempotency; the v340/v342 audit empty over the whole act; cards by kind unchanged by a telling; the two readings of "is this node an episode?" proved to be one seat, and proved to be two different QUESTIONS (the claim bound to nothing while its node is an episode); a vault with no identity records reading no episode anywhere and drawing the same tellings as an `event` (CERT-11); the belt drawing the node correctly, saying so by name, staying silent for an episode group, re-validating the repair, and still refusing `telling_count_disagrees` and `node_without_inputs`; and `CALCULATION_RULE_VERSION` proved not to move. Full local suite: 6785 tests, 6784 passed, 1 failed (the known macOS-only `test_file_answer_outer_queue_leaves_no_plaintext_temp`, which fails identically on a pristine tree), 4 skipped. Ruff parity held exactly: `temporal_projection.py`, `temporal_timeline.py`, `episode_fold.py`, `answer_placement.py` and `tests/test_temporal_projection.py` each match their v352 finding CLASSES with nothing new on either side, and the new test file carries only classes its v352 sibling already carries.
